guide.title: XML format contract
guide.summary: Draft ASM XML v1 grammar, cross-document rules, identity, and independent consumption.

section.title: Overview
section.p: This draft and schema/asm-v1.xsd define ASM XML. The schema defines document grammar; the rules here define corpus-level identity and reference semantics. The builder is a reference implementation, not a required dependency.

section.title: Documents
section.p: Documents are UTF-8 XML in namespace urn:asm:1, with version="1". The namespace is an identifier, not a network resource. Root kinds are symptom, diagnosis, intervention, and guide. Symptoms, diagnoses, and interventions live in matching plural directories under entries/. Guides live under guides/.

Document IDs are corpus-wide and case-sensitive. Symptom, diagnosis, and intervention IDs use S, D, or I followed by at least three digits. Guides use short kebab-case IDs. Documents carry title, summary, editorial status, and update date. Diagnostic entries also carry evidence. Diagnosis level and unit describe the assessed system; intervention targets name affected components.

section.title: Local identity
section.p: Only members of referenceable lists need local IDs. Use one to three lowercase words in kebab case, matching [a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z][a-z0-9]*){0,2}. IDs must be unique within the containing list, regardless of item tag. They are not XML xs:ID values, which would impose document-wide uniqueness.

The same ID may appear in a different list in the same document or in another document. Keep IDs stable when rearranging a list; order and identity are separate. Do not recycle an ID for a different meaning. Retain the source revision alongside an address when recording an assessment.
Singleton sections and containers have no IDs. Their tag names identify them.

section.title: Addresses
section.p: An address is a document ID, optionally followed by # and a slash-separated structural path. Each singleton contributes its tag name; a referenceable list member contributes its local ID in place of the repeated item tag.

tr.td: The singleton discriminator inside one alternative.

section.p: Inline ref target takes a fully qualified address, including for references inside the same document. Typed symptom-ref ref and intervention-ref ref target whole documents of the matching kind. Every reference must resolve. Relative or unqualified item names are not inferred.
Rendered fragments are the same scoped path after #. The source does not store fully qualified IDs or duplicate singleton tag names in ID attributes.

section.title: Symptom structure
section.p: observations contains one or more observation items with local IDs. benign-lookalikes contains individually addressable lookalike items. examples contains addressable example items with explicit kind: synthetic or observed. Notes can accompany lists without acquiring IDs.
how-to-recognize-it and what-to-record are singleton prose sections. Paragraphs inside them do not imply a list of separate observations or records. No section ID is needed.

section.title: Diagnosis structure
section.p: Required sections include definition, criteria, exclusions, differential, investigation, interventions, and evidence-and-uncertainty. Criteria, exclusions, and alternatives are lists of locally identified members. Each alternative has a singleton discriminator.

The criteria operator is all: all listed criteria must be supported to fit the working definition. This specifies combination, not an algorithm for assessing the prose. Missing information remains unknown. Differential alternatives are explanations to examine, not additional registered diagnoses.

section.title: Intervention structure
section.p: Required sections are purpose, preconditions, procedure, evaluation, risks-and-confounders, stop-and-rollback, and evidence-and-uncertainty. Preconditions and procedure steps are locally identified list members. Procedure order follows document order. Evaluation and rollback are singleton prose sections.

Applicability belongs to an intervention-ref in a diagnosis's relations list. It has a short local ID, a target document, a role (investigation, remediation, or both), an evidence label, and a required when condition. These conditions remain prose, not executable predicates. Duplicate entry-level typed relationships to the same target are invalid; a criterion's additional symptom reference is a distinct relationship.

section.title: Prose
section.p: Prose uses p, ul, ol, strong, em, code, and ref. Guides additionally use section titles, tables, and preformatted code blocks. Rich text preserves inline ordering and spaces. Generic bulleted prose does not create referenceable entities; use the semantic item elements when each member needs an address.

The a element is for external HTTP(S) or mailto links. All corpus navigation uses ref, so it is independent of source filenames and rendered paths. Renderers escape content and preserve references. A generated reading copy is never an editing source.

section.title: Validation
section.p: Validate against the local XSD, then check document IDs, directory agreement, local list uniqueness, and all references across the corpus. Reject IDs on singleton sections, duplicate IDs within one list, missing targets, wrong typed target kinds, unknown vocabulary, and unsupported namespace/version. Do not impose uniqueness across unrelated lists.

DTD and entity declarations, XInclude, network schema fetching, and executable content are unsupported. Consumers must not resolve external resources. Only UTF-8 is supported. Scientific validity and the truth of evidence labels require review beyond schema validation.

section.title: Outputs
section.p: The reference build writes disposable HTML, Markdown, and catalog.json into dist. The catalog contains document metadata, an ordered XML-derived tree, a qualified address index, and explicit relationships. Inline text and child nodes stay in order; indentation-only structural whitespace is omitted.

The index covers document roots, singleton sections, list containers, list items, and nested singleton discriminators. Each indexed address carries its owner, kind, source, and rendered URL. Relationships identify their nearest addressable owner, target, and type; intervention applicability additionally includes its own scoped address, condition, role, and evidence.
XML remains canonical. Independent tools need not run the reference builder. python examples/query_manual.py demonstrates direct reading with Python's standard library.

section.title: Evolution
section.p: This is a small draft contract. Update the schema, documentation, examples, and tests together. Before supporting external releases, define compatibility and release policy. Do not silently guess unsupported structures. There is no severity scale or executable diagnosis language in this format.
